value.body: Patent analysts search patent databases and scientific literature to judge whether an invention is new, who owns related patents, and where a technology is heading. IP law firms, patent research firms and the IP teams of R&D companies hire them. The day is mostly reading, searching and writing reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Science, pharmacy or engineering degree (BS-MS, M.Sc, B.Tech)

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Patent databases, literature search tools, Excel

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join IP research or law firms as analysts, usually tested on reading a patent and summarising it. Passing the Patent Agent Examination run by the Indian Patent Office allows registration as a patent agent later.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Domain knowledge in your science subject

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is for overseas clients, so it follows their patent systems too.
Next steps: senior analyst, patent agent, or IP manager.
The role keeps a science link but moves away from the lab bench.

value.title: Patent applications filed in India
value.note: Applications filed with the Indian Patent Office, not patents granted. More filings mean more search and analysis work, but not a fixed number of jobs.
